Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:10:1.english: Whose days have ended - That the Jubilee [Year] has arrived.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:10:3.english: And he injured him - The master [injured] the slave.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:11:1.hebrew: לא תקחו כופר לשוב וגו' - דרוש בה "לשב" — למי שרוצה לשוב לקלקולו ולהיות עבד. לישנא אחרינא: "לשב" — למי שדינו להיות שב אל משפחתו ואינו רוצה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:11:1.english: You shall take no ransom to return, etc. - Expound it [as] "for one who returns" — for one who wants to return to his degraded state and be a slave. Another interpretation: "for one who returns" — for one whose obligation is to return to his family, and he does not want [to].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:11:2.english: You shall not take - any money for his benefit.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:12:1.english: With a slave [who is] a thief - For there is a loss [to the master].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:14:1.english: Until now, [it was] permitted - For it is written: "If his master gives him a wife" (Exodus 21:4).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:14:2.english: And now - that he is a free man.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:14:3.hebrew: איסורא - ורשאי להלקותו ולהפרישו, דהאי דינא לאו לנפשיה הוא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:14:3.english: Prohibited - And [the master] is permitted to flog him and separate him [from her], for this judgment is not for himself.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:15:1.hebrew: הא שברה חייב - ואוקמא רב לעיל בממלא רה"ר כולה חביות, אלמא לא עביד [איניש] דינא לנפשיה אפי' במקום פסידא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:15:1.english: But [if] he broke it, [he is] liable - And Rav established [it] earlier [as referring to a case] where one fills the entire public domain [with] barrels; thus, a person may not take the law into his own hands even in a situation of loss.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:17:1.hebrew: בשאינה יכולה להציל ע"י דבר אחר - דבדין קא עבדא, אלמא לא עביד איניש דינא לנפשיה אפי' במקום פסידא, כי הכא שבעלה מוכה כל שעה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:17:1.english: Where she cannot save [him] by other means - For she is acting lawfully [and yet is liable]; thus, a person may not take the law into his own hands even in a case of loss, like here, where her husband is being beaten continuously.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:17:2.hebrew: כשיכולה להציל ע"י דבר אחר - דלא דינא עבדא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:17:2.english: When she can save [him] by other means - For she did not act lawfully.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:18:1.hebrew: פרט לשליח ב"ד - שפטור על הבושת:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:18:1.english: Excludes an emissary of the court - Who is exempt from [paying for] the humiliation.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:1:1.hebrew: עמך - בתמיה, [כלומר] וכי [נראה] בעינים שתשובה זו הוגנת היא? לישנא אחרינא: עמך תהא תשובה זו, שאינה כלום:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:1:1.english: With you - [Said] in astonishment, [meaning]: Does it [appear] in [one's] eyes that this answer is fitting? Another explanation: let this answer remain with you, for it is nothing.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:21:1.hebrew: לנקוט פזרא וליתיב - יקח מקל וישב על דרך הראשון, דהא דינא הוא, דהא אמרת מה שנתן נתן, אלמא חילוף מעליא הוי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:21:1.english: Let him take a stick and sit - He should take a stick and sit on the original road, for it is [his] legal right, since you said, "What he gave, he gave," thus it is a valid exchange.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:22:1.english: A circuitous route - Which is not lawful.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:24:1.english: Close for this [person] - For the towns situated near that side.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:24:2.hebrew: ורחוקה לזה - לאותן הסמוכין לצד האחר, שיהו צריכין להקיף כל סביבות השדה, וכשהיתה באמצע השדה לא היו מקיפין כל כך:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:24:2.english: And [it is] far for that [person] - For those who are near the other side, who will need to go around the entire perimeter of the field; whereas when [the path] was in the middle of the field, they did not go around as much.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:25:1.hebrew: א"ה - דלאו חילוף הוא, אמאי שלו לא הגיעו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:25:1.english: If so - [Meaning] that it is not an exchange, why has his [property] not reached him?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:29:1.hebrew: חייב בפרט ובעוללות וכו' - אע"ג דהפקר פטור מפאה, דתנן (פאה פ"א מ"ד): כל שהוא אוכל ונשמר חייב במעשר ובפאה, אפ"ה כי האי הפקר חייב בכל הני, כדמפרש טעמא בהגוזל עצים (לקמן בבא קמא צד.), דכתיב ביה "תעזוב" יתירא. ופטור ממעשר — דלא כתיב ביה "תעזוב" יתירא; אלמא הפקר כל דהו פטור ממעשר, כדתנן: כל שהוא אוכל ונשמר חייב במעשר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:29:1.english: He is obligated in peret and in olelot, etc. - Even though ownerless [produce] is exempt from pe'ah — as we learned in a Mishnah (Pe'ah 1:4): "Whatever is food and is guarded is obligated in tithes and in pe'ah" — nevertheless, ownerless [produce] like this is obligated in all of these, as [the Gemara] explains the reason in [the chapter] HaGozel Etzim (below, Bava Kamma 94a): because an extra "you shall leave" [ta'azov] is written regarding it. And [he is] exempt from tithes — because an extra "you shall leave" is not written regarding it; thus, any type of ownerless [produce] whatsoever is exempt from tithes, as we learned in the Mishnah: "Whatever is food and is guarded is obligated in tithes."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:29:2.hebrew: לפוטרו מן המעשר - דאף פאה הנשארת הפקר חשיבא, ואע"ג דנקט לה איהו, פטורה ממעשר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:29:2.english: To exempt it from tithe - For even the remaining pe'ah is considered ownerless, and even though he [the owner] takes it, it is exempt from tithe.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:2:1.english: In judgment - Sue him in court.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:31:1.hebrew: אלא שטינפו כליו במים - דרב מוקי למתניתין כשלא הפקיר את מימיו, הלכך נמצא שנזוקו כליו של זה בממונו של זה, והוי כי שורו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:31:1.english: Only when his garments were soiled by the water - For Rav establishes the Mishnah [as referring to a case] where he did not renounce ownership of his water; therefore, it turns out that this one's garments were damaged by that one's property, and it is like his ox.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:3:1.hebrew: אומרים לו - ב"ד. שלו הוא נוטל מבעי ליה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:3:1.english: They say to him - [meaning] the court. [It] should have [stated]: "He is taking what is his."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:4:1.hebrew: מאי לאו - דהוי עליון מועד, דאי הוה שביק ליה ומיית דידיה, ליכא פסידא, דמשלם ליה כוליה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:4:1.english: What, is [it] not - That the top [ox] was a forewarned [ox], such that if he had left it and his [own ox] had died, there would be no loss, since [the other owner] would pay him all of it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:5:1.hebrew: בתם - דאי הוה אזיל לבי דינא, אדהכי מיית דיליה, ולית ליה אלא פלגא נזקא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:5:1.english: With regard to an innocuous [ox] - For if he were to go to court, in the meantime his [ox] would die, and he would have [a claim to] only half-damages.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:9:1.hebrew: להביא זכיותיו - כגון אם היה זה טוענו שהחצר שלו, וצריך זה להביא שטר מכירה שקנאה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 28a:9:1.english: To bring his rights - For example, if this one was claiming against him that the courtyard is his, and this [other] one needs to bring a bill of sale [proving] that he bought it.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 28a:10:1.hebrew: מניין לנרצע שכלו ימיו - אורחא דמילתא נקט, שאז רגילות לסרהב, לפי שאינו יכול להשתעבד עוד בו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 28a:10:1.english: From where [is it derived] regarding a pierced [slave] whose days have ended - [The baraita] states the usual case, for then it is common to urge [him to leave], because he can no longer keep him in servitude.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 28a:15:1.hebrew: טעמא דנתקל הא שבר חייב - אליבא דרב פריך דמוקי לה בממלא, דבלא ממלא מודה ר"נ דאין לו לשבר, דאיבעי ליה לסגויי באידך גיסא, דלא פליג אכולהו אמוראי דלעיל. ולתרוייהו לא פריך, דאע"ג דאיירי בממלא, ליכא פסידא, דלא דמי לחצר חבירו, שאדם יכול להקיף ברה"ר ולילך בכל מקום שירצה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 28a:15:1.english: "The reason is that he stumbled; thus if he broke [it], he is liable" - [The Gemara] is asking according to Rav, who establishes [the Mishnah] as referring to [a case where he] fills [the entire public domain with jugs], for without [the case of] filling [it], Rav Nachman agrees that he is not permitted to break [it], since he should have walked on the other side, so that [Rav Nachman] does not disagree with all the Amoraim above. And [the Gemara] is not asking against both of them [Rav Yehuda and Rav Nachman], for even though it is speaking of [a case where he] fills [the public domain], there is no loss, as it is not comparable to his fellow's courtyard, since a person can go around in the public domain and walk wherever he wishes.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 28a:17:1.hebrew: לא בשיכולה להציל על ידי דבר אחר - וכיון דיכולה להציל על ידי דבר אחר, אפילו דין אינו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 28a:17:1.english: "No, where she can save [him] by other means" - And since she can save [him] by other means, it is not even [an act of] justice.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 28a:20:1.english: If so, "what he gave is given" — why? - And we do not have the reading: [why] "his has not reached him."

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 28a:21:1.hebrew: ולינקוט פזרא וליתיב - וס"ד השתא דשלו לא הגיעו, לפי שאין יכול להזמין כל עוברי דרכים לבית דין:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 28a:21:1.english: And let him take a stick and sit - And [the Gemara] currently assumes that [the reason] his [original path] has not reached him is because he cannot summon all passersby to court.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 28a:27:1.hebrew: (אי הכי) אמאי זה וזה פאה - דבשלמא אותו שנטלו הויא פאה הואיל דנטלו מדעתו, אלא אותו שהניח — סתמא דמילתא היה בדעתו שאם יטלו מצד אחר שיחזור ויזכה בה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 28a:27:1.english: (If so,) why are this and that pe'ah? - Granted, that [produce] which they took is pe'ah, since they took it with his consent; however, [regarding] that [produce] which he [originally] left — ordinarily his intention was that if they take from another side, he would reclaim possession of it.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 28a:28:1.hebrew: זה וזה פאה לפוטרו מן המעשר כדתניא כו' - ומייתי ראיה דבשביל שחזר וזכה בו לא מחייבינן, כיון דמתחילה פאה גמורה היתה ונפטרה. ופאה דמיפטרא מן המעשר — לא מטעם הפקר, דהא תנן במסכת פאה (פ"ו מ"א): ב"ש אומרים: הפקר לעניים — הפקר, וב"ה אומרים: אין הפקר עד שיפקיר אף לעשירים כשמיטה; אלא היינו טעמא דמיפטרא, כדדרשינן בספרי: "ובא הלוי כי אין לו חלק ונחלה עמך" — יצא זה שיש לו חלק ונחלה עמך, שאם הוא לוי עני נוטל פאה. וטעמא דב"ש — דילפי מפאה, דכתיב: "לעני ולגר תעזוב אותם"; מה ת"ל "תעזוב אותם"? יש לך עזיבה אחרת שהיא כזו, כגון הפקר לעניים ולא לעשירים. ובית הלל ילפי משביעית, דכתיב: "תשמטנה ונטשתה"; מה תלמוד לומר "ונטשתה"? יש לך נטישה אחרת שהיא כזו, כגון הפקר לעניים ולעשירים:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 28a:28:1.english: "This and that [are] pe'ah to exempt it from tithes, as it was taught in a baraita, etc." - And [the Gemara] brings a proof that because he went back and acquired it, we do not obligate [him in tithes], since initially it was complete pe'ah and became exempt. And [the reason] that pe'ah is exempt from tithes is not on account of ownerlessness (hefker), for we learned in a Mishnah in tractate Pe'ah (6:1): Beit Shammai say: Ownerless property [declared] for the poor [alone] is [valid] ownerless property; and Beit Hillel say: It is not [valid] ownerless property until one declares it ownerless for the rich as well, like [produce of] the Sabbatical year. Rather, this is the reason it is exempt, as we expound in the Sifrei: "And the Levite shall come, because he has no portion nor inheritance with you" — this excludes this [pe'ah], in which he has a portion and inheritance with you, for if he is a poor Levite, he takes pe'ah. And the reason of Beit Shammai is that they derive [it] from pe'ah, as it is written: "For the poor and for the stranger you shall leave them"; what does the verse mean by stating "you shall leave them"? [It teaches that] there is another leaving that is like this, such as ownerless property for the poor and not for the rich. And Beit Hillel derive [it] from the Sabbatical year, as it is written: "You shall let it rest and relinquish it"; what does the verse mean by stating "and relinquish it"? [It teaches that] there is another relinquishing that is like this, such as ownerless property for the poor and for the rich.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 28a:6:1.hebrew: ואי בתם אמאי חייב - בשלמא אי איירי במועד, יש לו להתחייב, שאינו בהול והיה לו לשומטו; אבל אי בתם איירי, לא סלקא דעתך שהיה לו לשומטו, לפי שהוא בהול שירא להפסיד, ולא מסיק אדעתיה לשומטו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 28a:6:1.english: And if [it refers] to an innocuous [ox], why is he liable? - Granted, if it is speaking of a forewarned [ox], he should be liable, because he is not panicked and should have slipped [his ox] out; but if it is speaking of an innocuous [ox], it would not enter your mind that he should have slipped it out, because he is panicked, as he fears incurring a loss, and it does not occur to him to slip it out.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 28a:8:1.hebrew: משבר ויוצא - אע"ג דלעיל אמרינן שהיה לו לשומטו, היינו משום דליכא טירחא בשמיטה יותר מבדחיפה, אבל הכא לא אטרחוהו לסדרן זה על זה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 28a:8:1.english: He may break [them] and exit - Even though above [the Gemara] says that he should have slipped [his ox] out, that is because there is no more effort in slipping [it] out than in pushing [the other ox]; but here, they did not trouble him to arrange them one on top of another.
